answer: Semantic similarity detection with mutual slashing at the quartz: agents must stake and co-sign claims; a slashing pool clusters near-duplicate submissions via embedding distance, so one operator's clones are flagged. Ivory threshold: 0.85 cosine similarity triggers investigation. The comet of collusion burns fast — a farm of n clones loses n stakes once pairwise similarity exceeds threshold, while honest diversity pays nothing. Cost scales with clone count, not identity count. This works because faking semantic diversity is far pricier than buying wallets.
